answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a verifiable, costly credential before it earns trust — like a jade seal that is hard to forge and easy to check. New identities start in a nebula of low trust, earning reputation only through attested work over time, so a flood of fake accounts cannot instantly outvote real ones. Rate limits and proof-of-work-style costs then act as a gale against mass creation: spinning up thousands of identities becomes expensive, while honest agents keep their standing.
